subject: maths
title: Money: Coins, Notes and Giving Change
seo_title: Year 2 Money Worksheets: Coins, £ and p, Adding and Change
standard_text: Recognise and use symbols for pounds (£) and pence (p); combine amounts to make a particular value; find different combinations of coins that equal the same amounts of money; solve simple problems in a practical context involving addition and subtraction of money of the same unit, including giving change.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on money: recognise UK coins and notes, use £ and p, count coins, find different ways to make 25p or £15, add prices at the tuck shop and give change from 50p or £1 by counting on. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Read the number on each coin, then count on from the biggest.
key_sub: £1 = 100p. Write pence as 50p and pounds as £5. To give change, count on from the price: 35p to 50p is 15p.
body_html:
Pounds and pence

We write pence with a small p: 50p. We write pounds with the £ sign in front: £5. £1 is the same as 100p.

A big coin is not always worth more. The 2p coin is bigger than the 5p coin, but 5p is worth more. Always read the number.

Count the coins, biggest first

Put the coins in order. Start with the biggest value and count on.

Example

Find two ways to make 30p.

20p + 10p = 30p. 10p + 10p + 10p = 30p. 20p + 10p uses the fewest coins.

Answer: 20p + 10p or 10p + 10p + 10p

Example

Add 35p + 20p.

Add the tens: 35p, 45p, 55p.

Answer: 55p

Give change by counting on

Start at the price. Count on to the money you paid. The jumps are the change.

Example

A drink costs 65p. You pay with a £1 coin. What is the change?

£1 = 100p. 65p + 5p = 70p. 70p + 30p = 100p. 5p + 30p = 35p.

Answer: 35p

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
4 coins, so 4pCount the value of each coin: 20p, 40p, 50p, 52p
£5 is the same as 5p£5 is five pounds. £1 alone is 100p
85p written as £85Pence have p after the number: 85p
Change from 50p for 35p is 25pCount on: 35p + 5p = 40p, 40p + 10p = 50p. The change is 15p

faq.q: What should a Year 2 child know about money?
faq.a: In the National Curriculum, Year 2 pupils use the £ and p symbols, count coins and notes, find different ways to make the same amount, and add and subtract money to work out change.
There are 100 pence in £1. So two 50p coins, five 20p coins or ten 10p coins all make £1.

faq.q: How do you teach a Year 2 child to give change?
faq.a: Count on from the price to the money paid. For 35p paid with 50p: 35p to 40p is 5p, 40p to 50p is 10p, so the change is 15p.

faq.q: Why does my child think the 2p coin is worth more than the 5p coin?
faq.a: The 2p coin is bigger, and young children often judge by size. Ask them to read the number on each coin before they count.

items.q: How much is this coin worth?
items.e: The coin says 10p. The p means pence. It is worth 10p.

items.q: How much is this coin worth?
items.e: The coin says 2p. It is worth 2p (2 pence). The £2 coin is gold and silver.

items.q: How much is this coin worth?
items.e: The coin says 50p. It is worth 50p (50 pence). There is no £50 coin.

items.q: How much is this coin worth?
items.e: This gold coin is £1 (one pound). £1 is worth 100p.

items.q: How much is this coin worth?
items.e: This gold and silver coin is £2 (two pounds). It is not 2p.

items.q: How much is this note worth?
items.e: This note says £5. It is worth £5 (five pounds).

items.q: How do you write 20 pence?
items.e: Write the number, then p for pence: 20p. £20 would be 20 pounds.

items.q: How do you write 5 pounds?
items.e: Write the £ sign first, then the number: £5. 5p would be 5 pence.

items.q: In £5, what does the £ sign mean?
items.e: £ means pounds. p means pence. £5 is five pounds.

items.q: How many pence make £1?
items.e: £1 = 100p. A £1 coin is worth the same as one hundred 1p coins.

items.q: Which coin is worth the most?
items.e: Look at the numbers, not the size. 20p is worth the most: 20p. The 2p coin is big, but it is only worth 2p.

items.q: Which coin is worth the most?
items.e: Pounds are worth more than pence. £2 = 200p, which is more than 50p. The answer is £2.

items.q: Which coin is worth the least?
items.e: The smallest number is 1. The 1p coin is worth the least.

items.q: The 2p coin is bigger than the 5p coin. Which coin is worth more?
items.e: Size does not matter. 5p is more than 2p, so the 5p coin is worth more.

items.q: Which of these is a note?
items.e: Notes are made of paper or plastic: £5, £10 and £20. £10 is a note. £1 and £2 are coins.

items.q: Which is worth more: 50p or £1?
items.e: £1 = 100p. 100p is more than 50p, so £1 is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth more: £2 or 20p?
items.e: 20 is a bigger number, but £2 is two pounds. £1 is already more than 20p, so £2 is worth more.

items.q: Which coin is worth the same as two 5p coins?
items.e: 5p + 5p = 10p. Two 5p coins are worth the same as one 10p coin.

items.q: How many 10p coins make £1?
items.e: £1 = 100p. Count in 10s: 10p, 20p, 30p … 100p. That is 10 coins.

items.q: Put these in order. Start with the least: £2, 5p, 50p.
items.e: Pence come first: 5p is less than 50p. £2 is two pounds, so it is the most. Order: 5p, 50p, £2.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each coin is 10p. Count in 10s: 10p, 20p, 30p, 40p. That is 40p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Charlie has these coins. How much does he have?
items.e: Each coin is 5p. Count in 5s: 5p, 10p, 15p, 20p, 25p. That is 25p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Jack finds these coins in his pencil case. How much is it?
items.e: Each coin is 2p. Count in 2s: 2p, 4p, 6p, 8p. That is 8p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each coin is 20p. Count in 20s: 20p, 40p, 60p. That is 60p.

items.q: Arjun puts this money in his money box. How much is in the box?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 10p, 20p, 21p, 22p, 23p. That is 23p.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 20p, 30p, 35p. That is 35p.

items.q: Maya has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 50p, 60p, 70p. That is 70p.

items.q: Grace finds these coins in her pencil case. How much is it?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 20p, 40p, 45p, 47p. That is 47p.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 50p, 70p, 75p, 76p. That is 76p.

items.q: Ruby puts this money in her money box. How much is in the box?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 10p, 20p, 30p, 32p, 34p. That is 34p.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 50p, 70p, 90p, 92p, 93p. That is 93p.

items.q: Zara has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 50p, 55p, 60p, 62p. That is 62p.

items.q: Kai finds these coins in his pencil case. How much is it?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 20p, 40p, 50p, 55p, 57p, 59p. That is 59p.

items.q: How many pence is this?
items.e: Each coin is 50p. Count in 50s: 50p, 100p. That is 100p. 100p is the same as £1.

items.q: How many pence is this?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 50p, 70p, 90p, 100p. That is 100p. 100p is the same as £1.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each coin is £1. Count in 1s: £1, £2, £3. That is £3. £3 is 3 pounds, not 3p.

items.q: Alfie has these coins. How much does he have?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: £2, £4, £5. That is £5. £5 is 5 pounds, not 5p.

items.q: Aisha puts this money in her money box. How much is in the box?
items.e: Start with the biggest note and count on: £5, £7, £8. That is £8. £8 is 8 pounds, not 8p.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Start with the biggest note and count on: £10, £15, £17. That is £17. £17 is 17 pounds, not 17p.

items.q: Mohammed puts this money in his money box. How much is in the box?
items.e: Start with the biggest note and count on: £10, £15, £17, £18, £19. That is £19. £19 is 19 pounds, not 19p.

items.q: Which coins make 25p?
items.e: 20p + 5p = 25p. 20p + 2p + 1p is only 23p.

items.q: Which coins make 30p?
Which coins make 50p?
Which coins make 17p?
Which coins make 64p?
Which of these does NOT make 20p?
items.e: 10p + 5p + 2p = 17p, not 20p. The others all make 20p. So the answer is 10p + 5p + 2p.

items.q: Which of these does NOT make 40p?
items.e: 20p + 10p + 5p = 35p, not 40p. There are many ways to make 40p, but not 20p + 10p + 5p.

items.q: Which of these does NOT make £10?
Which notes and coins make £15?
Which notes and coins make £20?
items.e: £10 + £10 = £20. There is also a £20 note.

items.q: Which coin do you add to make 35p?
items.e: 20p + 10p = 30p. 30p + 5p = 35p. Add a 5p coin.

items.q: Which coin do you add to make 75p?
items.e: 50p + 20p = 70p. 70p + 5p = 75p. Add a 5p coin.

items.q: Which coin do you add to make 27p?
items.e: 10p + 10p + 5p = 25p. 25p + 2p = 27p. Add a 2p coin.

items.q: Which coin do you add to make £1?
Which coin do you add to make £15?
What is the fewest coins you need to make 30p?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can first: 20p + 10p = 30p. That is 2 coins. There is no 30p coin, so 1 coin cannot work.

items.q: What is the fewest coins you need to make 70p?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can first: 50p + 20p = 70p. That is 2 coins.

items.q: What is the fewest coins you need to make 9p?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can first: 5p + 2p + 2p = 9p. That is 3 coins. There is no 4p coin, so you need two 2p coins.

items.q: What is the fewest coins you need to make 80p?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can first: 50p + 20p + 10p = 80p. That is 3 coins.

items.q: What is the fewest notes and coins you need to make £8?
items.e: Use the biggest note or coin you can first: £5 + £2 + £1 = £8. That is 3 notes and coins.
Add the tens, then the ones: 20p + 30p = 50p. The total is 50p.
Add the tens, then the ones: 15p + 10p = 25p. The total is 25p.
Add the tens, then the ones: 40p + 20p = 60p, 60p + 5p = 65p. The total is 65p.
Add the tens, then the ones: 35p + 20p = 55p. The total is 55p.
Add the tens, then the ones: 38p + 20p = 58p, 58p + 5p = 63p. The total is 63p. The ones make more than 10, so exchange 10 ones for 1 ten.
Add the tens, then the ones: 47p + 30p = 77p, 77p + 6p = 83p. The total is 83p. The ones make more than 10, so exchange 10 ones for 1 ten.
Add the tens, then the ones: 55p + 40p = 95p, 95p + 5p = 100p. The total is 100p. 100p is the same as £1. The ones make more than 10, so exchange 10 ones for 1 ten.
Add one price at a time: 12p, 27p, 47p. The total is 47p.

items.q: At the tuck shop, Ethan buys an apple and a carton of milk. How much does he spend?
items.e: Add the tens, then the ones: 20p + 30p = 50p. The total is 50p.

items.q: At the tuck shop, Amelia buys some toast and a biscuit. How much does she spend?
items.e: Add the tens, then the ones: 25p + 10p = 35p, 35p + 5p = 40p. The total is 40p.

items.q: At the tuck shop, Lily buys a juice and some toast. How much does she spend?
items.e: Add the tens, then the ones: 40p + 20p = 60p, 60p + 5p = 65p. The total is 65p.

items.q: At the tuck shop, Poppy buys a carton of milk and a juice. How much does she spend?
items.e: Add the tens, then the ones: 30p + 40p = 70p. The total is 70p.

items.q: At the tuck shop, Ava buys an apple, some toast and a biscuit. How much does she spend?
items.e: Add one price at a time: 20p, 45p, 60p. The total is 60p.

items.q: At the tuck shop, Charlie buys a biscuit, a carton of milk and a juice. How much does he spend?
items.e: Add one price at a time: 15p, 45p, 85p. The total is 85p.
Add the pounds: 6 + 8 = 14. The total is £14. The answer is in pounds, not pence.
Add the pounds: 10 + 5 = 15. The total is £15. The answer is in pounds, not pence.

items.q: At the toy shop, Jack buys a ball and a toy car. How much does he spend?
items.e: Add the prices: £4 + £3 = £7.

items.q: At the toy shop, Leo buys a kite and a book. How much does he spend?
items.e: Add the prices: £7 + £5 = £12.

items.q: At the toy shop, Arjun buys a game and a kite. How much does he spend?
items.e: Add the prices: £9 + £7 = £16.

items.q: At the toy shop, Harry buys a toy car, a game and a book. How much does he spend?
items.e: Add one price at a time: £3, £12, £17. The total is £17.

items.q: Maya buys a sweet for 6p. She pays with a 10p coin. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count on from 6p to 10p: 6p + 4p = 10p. The change is 4p. Check: 6p + 4p = 10p.

items.q: Grace buys a sticker for 15p. She pays with a 20p coin. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count on from 15p to 20p: 15p + 5p = 20p. The change is 5p. Check: 15p + 5p = 20p.

items.q: Evie buys a lolly for 35p. She pays with a 50p coin. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count on from 35p to 50p: 35p + 5p = 40p, 40p + 10p = 50p. Add the jumps: 5p + 10p = 15p. The change is 15p. Check: 35p + 15p = 50p. It is not 25p: 35p + 25p = 60p.

items.q: Ruby buys an apple for 40p. She pays with a £1 coin. How much change does she get?
items.e: £1 = 100p. Count on from 40p to 100p: 40p + 60p = 100p. The change is 60p. Check: 40p + 60p = 100p.

items.q: Noah buys a bag of crisps for 65p. He pays with a £1 coin. How much change does he get?
items.e: £1 = 100p. Count on from 65p to 100p: 65p + 5p = 70p, 70p + 30p = 100p. Add the jumps: 5p + 30p = 35p. The change is 35p. Check: 65p + 35p = 100p. It is not 45p: 65p + 45p = 110p.

items.q: Zara buys a bottle of water for 72p. She pays with a £1 coin. How much change does she get?
items.e: £1 = 100p. Count on from 72p to 100p: 72p + 8p = 80p, 80p + 20p = 100p. Add the jumps: 8p + 20p = 28p. The change is 28p. Check: 72p + 28p = 100p.

items.q: Kai gets £2 pocket money each week. How much does he have after 5 weeks?
items.e: Count in 2s: £2, £4, £6, £8, £10. That is £10. £7 comes from adding 2 + 5.

items.q: Oliver has £10. He buys a book for £6. How much money is left?
items.e: £10 − £6 = £4. Count on: £6 to £10 is £4. £16 adds instead of taking away.

items.q: A toy car costs £8. George has £5. How much more money does he need?
items.e: Count on from £5 to £8: £6, £7, £8. That is £3 more.

items.q: Freya has 45p. Her gran gives her 30p. How much does she have now?
items.e: 45p + 30p: 45p, 55p, 65p, 75p. That is 75p. 15p takes away instead of adding.

items.q: At the tuck shop, Alfie buys a biscuit for 15p and a carton of milk for 30p. He pays with a 50p coin. How much change does he get?
items.e: Cost: 15p + 30p = 45p. Count on from 45p to 50p: 5p. 45p is the cost, not the change.

items.q: Apples cost 20p each. Aisha buys 2 apples. How much does she pay?
Pencils cost 10p each. How many pencils can Isla buy with 50p?
items.e: Count in 10s to 50p: 10p, 20p, 30p, 40p, 50p. That is 5 pencils.

items.q: Mohammed has three 20p coins. He spends 45p. How much money is left?
items.e: Three 20p coins: 20p, 40p, 60p. Count on from 45p to 60p: 45p + 5p = 50p, 50p + 10p = 60p. 5p + 10p = 15p is left.

items.q: A comic costs £4. Ethan pays with a £10 note. How much change does he get?
Amelia has £20. She buys a game for £12 and a ball for £5. How much money is left?
items.e: Spent: £12 + £5 = £17. Count on from £17 to £20: £3 is left. £8 only takes away the game.

items.q: At the school fair, cakes cost 25p each. Lily buys 2 cakes and a juice for 30p. How much does she spend?
items.e: Cakes: 25p + 25p = 50p. Add the juice: 50p + 30p = 80p. 55p is only 1 cake.

items.q: Poppy has 50p. Crisps cost 30p and a juice costs 25p. Can she buy both?
items.e: Cost: 30p + 25p = 55p. 55p is more than 50p, so no. 50p + 5p = 55p, so she needs 5p more.

items.q: Ava has two £5 notes and three £1 coins. How much money does she have?
items.e: £5 + £5 = £10. Then £11, £12, £13. That is £13. £5 counts the notes and coins, not their value.

items.q: Charlie buys a drink for 30p. He pays with a £1 coin. Which coins could he get as change?
items.e: £1 = 100p. Count on from 30p to 100p: 70p. 50p + 20p = 70p, so 50p + 20p.
